mainTopic: Which פסול items stay on the מזבח once they went up: ריש לקיש's chart, the משנה of 'אם עלו לא ירדו', and the ברייתא's source from "זאת תורת העולה"
overview: This amud finishes ריש לקיש's chart of which פסול מנחות and נסכים stay on the מזבח once they went up, according to רבן גמליאל, רבי יהושע, רבי שמעון and the others. The גמרא asks why such a chart was needed. It answers that the chart shows a מנחה can come by itself, like רבא's rule. The chart also shows that נסכים brought on a later day, after their animal, still count as coming with the זבח. Then a new משנה lists פסול offerings that are not taken down once on the מזבח. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about three more cases. רבי שמעון's rule is that a problem which began in holiness is accepted by the מזבח, while animals that were unfit from the start come down. The משנה adds that whatever came down is not brought back up, and a live animal always comes down. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא showing how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון each read the פסוק "זאת תורת העולה". It begins to explain why one group is included and the other left out, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A meal offering that comes with an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes the case before this one, then rules on a מנחה that comes with a זבח: according to רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע it stays up; according to everyone else it comes down.
steps.simpleTranslation: …it comes down. A מנחה that comes with an animal offering: according to רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע it does not come down; according to everyone else it comes down.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is going through the opinions one by one, telling us what happens to a פסול item that already went up on the מזבח. Here he deals with a מנחה that is brought together with an animal קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first word 'תרד' finishes the case that came right before this section. Then a new case starts. רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע say this מנחה stays on the מזבח once it went up. The other תנאים say it must be taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall come down (be taken off the מזבח)
A flour offering
That comes together with an animal offering
According to everyone (all the other opinions)

phrases.english: shall descend.
phrases.notes: This word finishes the case that came just before this section.

phrases.english: A meal offering that comes with an animal offering:
according to the words of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua,
it shall not descend;
according to the words of everyone else, it shall descend.
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' here means all the other תנאים in the discussion, not the two just named.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's summary that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסול מנחה brought with a זבח: according to רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע it stays up; according to the other תנאים it comes down.

steps.title: Libations alone and libations with an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: נסכים that come alone: according to most opinions they come down, but according to רבן גמליאל and רבי שמעון they stay up. נסכים that come with a זבח: according to everyone they come down, except רבן גמליאל alone, who says they stay up.
steps.simpleTranslation: נסכים that come by themselves: according to everyone they come down; according to רבן גמליאל and רבי שמעון they do not come down. נסכים that come with a זבח: according to everyone they come down; according to רבן גמליאל alone they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש continues his chart with the wine offerings (נסכים). He splits them into two cases: brought alone, or brought together with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For נסכים brought alone, רבי שמעון agrees with רבן גמליאל that they stay up. For נסכים brought with a זבח, רבי שמעון no longer agrees, so only רבן גמליאל says they stay up. That is why the text says 'רבן גמליאל alone.'

keyTerms.meaning: Wine offerings poured on the מזבח
By themselves, not tied to an animal offering
They shall come down
Alone, by himself

steps.whatToRemember: The full chart: the more an item stands on its own (not tied to a זבח), the more opinions say it stays on the מזבח. רבן גמליאל is the most lenient: anything meant for the fire stays up.

phrases.english: Libations that come by themselves:
according to the words of everyone, they shall descend;

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא יֵרְדוּ.
phrases.english: according to the words of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Shimon, they shall not descend.
Libations that come with an animal offering:
according to the words of everyone, they shall descend;

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְחוֹדֵיהּ לֹא יֵרְדוּ.
phrases.english: according to the words of Rabban Gamliel alone, they shall not descend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same summary, moving from מנחה to נסכים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים alone: they stay up only according to רבן גמליאל and רבי שמעון. נסכים with a זבח: they stay up only according to רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: Isn't this summary obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed to spell all this out, since it follows directly from the opinions already known.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: everything in his chart can be worked out from the opinions of the תנאים, so why say it? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the summary adds no new information. Each תנא's rule was already stated, so applying it to these cases seems to be simple arithmetic.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the summary in steps 1-2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each result follows directly from the known opinions, so the summary seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Needed for a meal offering that comes alone, like רבא
steps.stepSummary: The summary was needed to include the case of a מנחה that comes by itself. That case is real, as רבא teaches: a person may volunteer a מנחת נסכים on any day, even without an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed it for a מנחה that comes by itself, and this fits רבא, who said: a person may volunteer a מנחת נסכים any day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the summary does teach something. Mentioning a מנחה that 'comes by itself' tells us such a case exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מנחת נסכים goes along with an animal. רבא says a person may bring it alone as a donation on any day. ריש לקיש's list quietly agrees with this by treating 'a מנחה that comes by itself' as a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed it (to teach something)
Volunteers, donates
The flour offering that normally comes with the wine offerings

phrases.english: A meal offering that comes by itself
was necessary for him,
phrases.notes: He means this case is the reason ריש לקיש made the list.

phrases.english: and it is in line with Rava,
as Rava said:
A person may volunteer a meal offering of libations
on any day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement has a hidden teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a מנחה can come alone, following רבא.

steps.title: Then just quote רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if that is the point, ריש לקיש should simply have taught us רבא's rule directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him teach us that the law follows רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the goal was to show that a מנחה can come alone, a long chart is a strange way to say it. This prepares the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that the answer does not explain the whole list. In particular, it does not explain why the נסכים cases were included.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach us

phrases.english: Then let him teach us in line with Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the list was made to teach רבא's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the purpose, ריש לקיש could have stated רבא's rule outright instead of listing every case.

steps.title: Needed for libations brought with an animal, offered on a later day
steps.stepSummary: The list was also needed for נסכים that come with a זבח. Since such נסכים may be offered the next day or even later, after the animal, one could have thought they count as נסכים brought alone. The next step spells this out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed it for נסכים that come with a זבח, which a person may offer tomorrow or on some later day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the list also teaches something new about נסכים that belong to an animal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even נסכים that belong to a זבח do not have to be offered at the same time as the animal; they can be brought the next day or later. Because of that, one might mistakenly treat them as נסכים brought alone, so ריש לקיש needed to list this case. The next step explains the mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Offers, brings near
Tomorrow, the next day
On another (later) day

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's list is not just a recap. It hints that a מנחת נסכים can come alone (like רבא), and it shows that נסכים of a זבח still count as 'with the זבח' even when they are offered on a later day.

phrases.english: Libations that come with an animal offering
were necessary for him,
since he may offer them
the next day or on another day.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְסָכִים הַבָּאִים עִם הַזֶּבַח אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies an additional law hidden in the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list only repeats רבא and could have been replaced by quoting him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list was needed for נסכים of a זבח: even though they may be offered on a later day, they still count as coming with the זבח (as step 7 explains).

steps.title: Late libations still count as coming with the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the mistake ריש לקיש was preventing. One might think נסכים brought on a later day are like נסכים brought alone, so even רבי שמעון would agree they stay up. ריש לקיש teaches that this is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the Master learned from 'their מנחה and their נסכים' that נסכים may be brought at night and on a later day, such late נסכים are like נסכים that come by themselves, and רבי שמעון would agree they do not come down. So ריש לקיש teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 6. It spells out the mistaken idea that ריש לקיש's list was meant to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נסכים may be offered after their animal, at night or the next day. That might make them look like they are no longer tied to the זבח, which would put them under the rule for נסכים brought alone, where they stay up. ריש לקיש's list shows that even late נסכים still count as 'coming with a זבח,' so the stricter rule for that case applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
Their מנחה and their libations, the פסוק that allows late נסכים
By themselves, not tied to an animal offering
He comes to teach us (this point)

steps.whatToRemember: נסכים brought after their animal, even days later, still count as נסכים 'that come with a זבח.' This ends the discussion of ריש לקיש's list.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say,
since the Master said:
"Their meal offering and their libations" teaches that they may be brought at night,
and "their meal offering and their libations" teaches that they may be brought the next day,
so they are like libations that come by themselves,
and רבי שמעון would agree that they do not come down;
so he teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: Meaning: they still count as coming with the animal, so they follow that rule and come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the mistaken thought that the answer in Step 6 was meant to block.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a mistaken idea that the statement comes to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Late נסכים are treated like נסכים brought alone, so even רבי שמעון would agree they stay up.
steps.terutzMaskana: Late נסכים still count as coming with a זבח, so they follow that rule.

steps.title: Disqualified offerings that stay on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists disqualified offerings that are not taken down once they are on the מזבח: לן, יוצא, טמא, slaughtered with intent for outside its time or place, and blood received and sprinkled by unfit people.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These, if they went up, do not come down: what was left overnight, what went out of its area, what became impure, an animal slaughtered with intent for outside its time or place, and one whose blood unfit people received and sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists offerings that became disqualified, yet once they are on the מזבח they stay there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the offering is already פסול. The rule is only that once it reaches the מזבח, we do not take it down. The offering is not suddenly kosher. These cases are an exception in what happens next, not a change in their status.

keyTerms.meaning: If they went up onto the מזבח, they do not come down
Something left overnight off the מזבח
Something that went out of its proper area
Intent to offer or eat it beyond its time or outside its place
People who are unfit to do the עבודה

steps.confusionAlert: 'They do not come down' does not mean the offering is kosher. It is still פסול. We simply leave it on the מזבח once it is there.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
These, if they went up, shall not come down:
what was left overnight, what went out, and what became impure,
and what was slaughtered for beyond its time or outside its place,
phrases.notes: This means slaughtered with the plan to offer or eat it at the wrong time or in the wrong place.

phrases.english: and one whose blood unfit people received and sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. The earlier topic of נסכים is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These disqualified offerings stay on the מזבח once they have gone up.

steps.title: Three disputed cases: night, spilled blood, blood outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says an animal slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, or one whose blood went outside the curtains comes down. רבי שמעון says it stays up, because the problem happened in the holy service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if it was slaughtered at night, its blood spilled, or its blood went outside the curtains, then even if it went up, it comes down. רבי שמעון says: it does not come down, because its disqualification happened in the holy service.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreement about three more disqualified cases. Do they come down from the מזבח or stay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats these three cases as worse than the earlier list, so they come down. רבי שמעון puts them with the earlier list, because the problem happened during the holy service itself (פסולו בקודש).

keyTerms.meaning: Its blood spilled and was not caught in a כלי
Outside the curtains, meaning outside the courtyard
Its disqualification happened in the holy place or service

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
one that was slaughtered at night,
or whose blood was spilled,
or whose blood went out beyond the curtains —
if it went up, it comes down.
Rabbi Shimon says: it does not come down,
because its disqualification happened in holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disagreement about three more cases, beyond the agreed list in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: these three cases come down. רבי שמעון: they stay up, because the problem happened in holiness.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule: the holy place accepts what became unfit inside it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives his general rule. If an offering's problem happened inside the holy service, the מזבח accepts it. If the problem started before that, the מזבח does not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי שמעון says: anything whose disqualification happened in holiness, the holy place accepts. If its disqualification did not happen in holiness, the holy place does not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the reason behind רבי שמעון's view with a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is where the problem began. If it began during the עבודה, once the offering is on the מזבח it stays. If the animal was unfit from the start, before it ever entered the holy service, the מזבח does not hold onto it.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy place (the מזבח) accepts it, so it stays up
The holy place does not accept it, so it comes down

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the next list in the משנה, which names animals whose problem did not start in holiness.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon says:
anything whose disqualification happened in holiness,
the holy place accepts it;
if its disqualification did not happen in holiness,
the holy place does not accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁפְּסוּלוֹ בַּקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general reason for רבי שמעון's ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering whose problem happened in holiness stays on the מזבח. One whose problem did not happen in holiness comes down.

steps.title: Animals whose problem started before the holy service
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists animals whose disqualification did not happen in holiness: רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טריפה, יוצא דופן, and בעלי מומין. These come down even if they went up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones whose disqualification was not in holiness: an animal that mated with a person, one that a person mated with, one set aside for idol worship, one that was worshipped, a harlot's payment, the price of a dog, a mixed breed, a טריפה, one born by caesarean, and blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names the animals that were unfit before they ever came into the holy service. Under רבי שמעון's rule, the מזבח does not accept them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each problem here comes from the animal's life or birth, before it was offered, not from a mistake during the עבודה. Since the problem did not start in holiness, these animals come down from the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with
Set aside for idol worship, and actually worshipped
A harlot's payment, and the price of a dog
Born by caesarean section
Animals with a blemish

phrases.english: And these are the ones whose disqualification was not in holiness:
an animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with,
one set aside for idol worship, and one that was worshipped,
a harlot's payment, and the price of a dog,
an animal of mixed species, and a fatally wounded animal,
one born by caesarean section, and blemished animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the cases that fall under the second half of רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These animals were unfit before the holy service, so they come down even if they went up.

steps.title: Disagreement about blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that blemished animals stay up once they have gone up. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים reports that his father used to push blemished animals off the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא considers blemished animals fit to stay. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says: my father used to push blemished animals off the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a disagreement about the last item on the list, animals with a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a blemished animal, once on the מזבח, is not taken down. רבי חנינא brings a report of what was actually done in the מקדש, which supports the view that they do come down.

keyTerms.meaning: Considers it fit (here: it stays on the מזבח)
The deputy כהן גדול
Pushes away or removes

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's split: problems that began in holiness stay on the מזבח (according to רבי שמעון), and problems that began before the service come down. Blemished animals are disputed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva deems blemished animals fit.
phrases.notes: 'Fit' here means that if they went up onto the מזבח, they stay there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest, says:

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹחֶה הָיָה אַבָּא אֶת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
phrases.english: my father used to push blemished animals
off of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a disagreement about the last item, בעלי מומין, from the list in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: blemished animals stay up. רבי חנינא, reporting his father's practice: they are removed from the מזבח.

steps.title: What came down does not go back up
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a limit. The offerings that stay up once they went up are not brought back up if they came down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as these offerings do not come down if they went up, so too, if they came down, they do not go back up.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more rule about the disqualified offerings it listed earlier: the 'stay up' rule only protects them while they are already on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8 to 12 taught that certain disqualified offerings are not taken down once they are on the מזבח. This line teaches that the rule does not work backwards. If such an offering came down, nobody should bring it back up.

keyTerms.meaning: they come down (from the מזבח)
they go up (onto the מזבח)
just as... so too

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'stays up' means 'is fully kosher.' These offerings are still disqualified. The מזבח only holds on to them if they are already there.

phrases.english: Just as, if they went up, they do not come down,
so too, if they came down, they do not go up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the 'once up, stays up' rule from the earlier lines of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A disqualified offering that would stay up once on the מזבח is not brought back up if it came down.

steps.title: Live animals come down; a burnt offering slaughtered on top is handled there
steps.stepSummary: Any of these animals that went up alive must come down. A עולה that went up alive comes down, but if it was slaughtered on top of the מזבח, it is skinned and cut up right there.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of these animals, if they went up to the top of the מזבח alive, must come down. A עולה that went up alive to the top of the מזבח must come down. If someone slaughtered it on top of the מזבח, he should skin it and cut it into pieces where it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by teaching that the 'stays up' rule does not apply to a living animal. It then gives the case of a kosher עולה that was slaughtered on top of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח only holds on to an offering after it has been slaughtered, so a living animal is brought down. A kosher עולה is not supposed to be slaughtered up there in the first place. Still, if it already was slaughtered there, it is not brought down. The skinning and cutting are done right on the spot.

keyTerms.meaning: alive
the top of the מזבח
a burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
he skins it (removes the hide)
he cuts it into its parts

steps.whatToRemember: The 'stays up' rule only works for an animal that has already been slaughtered. A live animal always comes down.

phrases.english: And all of them that went up alive
to the top of the altar must come down.
A burnt offering that went up alive
to the top of the altar must come down.
If he slaughtered it on top of the altar,
he should skin it and cut it into pieces in its place.
phrases.notes: 'In its place' means right there on top of the מזבח, without bringing it down first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another limit on the 'once up, stays up' rule: it does not apply to living animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals that went up alive come down. A עולה slaughtered on top of the מזבח is skinned and cut up there.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's three limiting words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי יהודה reads three limiting words in the פסוק to exclude three cases from the 'stays up' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: 'This,' 'it,' and 'the burnt offering' are three limiting words. They exclude an animal slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood went outside the curtains. If one of these went up, it must come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that shows where רבי יהודה's view in the משנה (Step 9) comes from in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that teaches 'whatever goes up stays up' contains three small limiting words. רבי יהודה says each word cuts out one case, which gives exactly the three cases he listed in the משנה. So these three come down even if they went up.

keyTerms.meaning: a limiting word in the פסוק, used to exclude a case
except for, to exclude
the curtains, meaning the walls of the courtyard

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'This,' 'it,' 'the burnt offering'
these are three exclusions;
to exclude one that was slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood was spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains,
that if it went up, it must come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins, giving the פסוק source for רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three limiting words exclude an animal slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood left the courtyard. These come down even if they went up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the מחלוקת in the משנה is really a disagreement about how to read the פסוק, not only about reasoning.

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins: the word עולה includes disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the word עולה alone would only teach about a kosher עולה. He asks where we learn to include a long list of disqualified offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: from the word 'burnt offering' I would only know about a kosher עולה. From where do we learn to include one slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, one whose blood went outside the curtains, one left overnight, one taken out of the courtyard, one that became טמא, one slaughtered with intent for outside its time or its place, and one whose blood unfit people received and sprinkled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון starts his own reading of the same פסוק. He is setting up a question whose answer, from the פסוק, will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the פסוק to leave cases out. רבי שמעון uses it to bring cases in. His list includes רבי יהודה's three cases plus all the cases from the משנה in Step 8. This matches his rule that a problem which happened inside the holy service stays on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: kosher, fit
from where (do we learn)?
to include
left overnight past its time
people who are unfit to do the service

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מִנַּיִן' here is not a real challenge. רבי שמעון is setting up his own proof, and the answer from the פסוק comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: 'Burnt offering':
I have only a fit burnt offering;
from where do we include one slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood was spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains,
and one left overnight, and one taken out, and one that is impure,
and one slaughtered with intent for outside its time and outside its place,
and one where unfit people received and sprinkled its blood,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״עֹלָה״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹלָה כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's opposite reading of the same פסוק that רבי יהודה used in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון sets out to include many disqualified offerings in the 'once up, stays up' rule, including רבי יהודה's three cases.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's list continues: blood put in the wrong place
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's question goes on. It adds offerings whose blood was put above instead of below the line, below instead of above, inside instead of outside, or outside instead of inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and offerings whose blood should be placed below but was placed above, and blood that should be above but was placed below, and offerings whose blood should be placed outside but was placed inside, and inside but was placed outside...
steps.whatsHappening: The same question from רבי שמעון keeps going, adding cases where the blood was put in the wrong spot. The answer has not come yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these mistakes happen during the blood service itself, which is inside the holy service. That is why רבי שמעון wants to include them too, so they stay up once they are on the מזבח. 'Above' and 'below' refer to the line around the outer מזבח. 'Inside' and 'outside' mean the inner היכל versus the outer מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: those (offerings) whose blood is supposed to be placed
below / above (the line around the מזבח)
outside (on the outer מזבח) / inside (in the היכל)

phrases.english: those placed below that one placed above,
phrases.notes: There was a red line around the middle of the outer מזבח. Some blood goes below it and some goes above it.

phrases.english: and above that one placed below,
and those placed outside that one placed inside,
inside that one placed outside,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list in רבי שמעון's question from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון also wants to include offerings whose blood was placed in the wrong spot (above/below or inside/outside) in the 'stays up' rule.

steps.title: Last case on the list, and the answer from the words "The law of the עולה"
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון adds a פסח and a חטאת slaughtered for the wrong purpose to his list. He answers that "תורת העולה" makes one rule for everything that goes up: once it went up, it does not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a פסח or a חטאת that was slaughtered for the wrong purpose: where do we learn that it stays up? The פסוק says "The law of the עולה." It made one law for everything that goes up on the מזבח: if it went up, it does not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds one last case to his long question. Then he gives the answer: the words "תורת העולה" cover every one of these offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "עולה" alone would only teach about a kosher עולה. רבי שמעון reads "תורת" (the law of) as one single law for everything that goes up. So all the disqualified offerings from steps 16 and 17 also stay up once they are on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The Passover offering
A sin offering
Not for their own sake: slaughtered with the wrong purpose in mind
The פסוק teaches: this introduces the source
It included: the פסוק widens the rule to cover more cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the rule that many disqualified offerings are not taken down from the מזבח once they are on it.

phrases.english: And a פסח and a חטאת
that were slaughtered not for their own sake: from where do we learn this?
The פסוק says: "The law of the עולה"
It included one law for everything that goes up
that if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רבי שמעון's question from steps 16 and 17 and gives his answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that disqualified offerings, including a פסח or חטאת slaughtered for the wrong purpose, stay on the מזבח?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From "תורת העולה": one law for everything that goes up. Once it went up, it does not come down.

steps.title: The word "This" leaves out a different group of animals
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think the inclusion also covers animals like a רובע, a מוקצה, an אתנן or a טרפה. The word "זאת" leaves them out, so these come down even if they went up.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think I should also include an animal that mated with a person or that a person mated with, one set aside for or worshipped as idol worship, a harlot's payment or a dog's price, a mixed breed, a טרפה, or one born by caesarean. So the פסוק says "זאת" (this), to leave them out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון puts a limit on the wide rule he just learned. The word "זאת" leaves out a list of animals that are not covered by the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תורת" made the rule wide, so we might think every bad animal is included. "זאת" (this) narrows it again, and these animals are taken down even if they went up. This step only says which animals are left out. The next step asks for the reason behind the split, and the answer begins in step 21 and continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with
An animal set aside for idol worship, and one worshipped as a god
An animal given as a harlot's payment, and one traded for a dog
An animal born from two different species
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
An animal born by caesarean section

steps.confusionAlert: Both the inclusion ("תורת") and the exclusion ("זאת") come from the same פסוק. Do not mix up the two lists: step 18's offerings stay up, but this step's animals come down.

phrases.english: I might think that I should include
an animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with
and one set aside for idol worship, and one that was worshipped
and a harlot's payment and a dog's price
and a mixed breed, a טרפה, and one born by caesarean section?
The פסוק says: "This."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק as before: "זאת תורת העולה". The word "this" limits the rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the wide inclusion from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "זאת" leaves out a רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טרפה and יוצא דופן. They come down even if they went up.

steps.title: Why include the first group and leave out the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason there is to include the first list and leave out the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what reason did you see to include those and to leave out these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next move. Why does "תורת" include the first group while "זאת" leaves out the second group?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both groups are disqualified animals, and the פסוק has words for including and for leaving out. The question asks what makes the first group fit the inclusion and the second group fit the exclusion. Without a reason, the split could just as well go the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see: what reason do you have
To include
To leave out, to exclude

phrases.english: And what reason did you see
to include those
phrases.notes: "Those" are the offerings from steps 16 to 18, which stay up.

phrases.english: and to leave out these?
phrases.notes: "These" are the animals from the last step, like a רובע or a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומה ראית לרבות את אלו ולהוציא את אלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the split between steps 18 and 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason decides which disqualified animals are included (stay up) and which are left out (come down)?

steps.title: The answer begins: "After it included"
steps.stepSummary: The answer to why one group is included and the other left out starts here. It goes on in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the פסוק included...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to the question in step 20. Only the opening words are here; the rest comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer opens by pointing back to the inclusion ("רִיבָּה") the פסוק already made. The full reason for the split between the two groups is given in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: After that: opens an answer built on what was already said
An inclusion: a word in the פסוק that widens a rule
An exclusion: a word in the פסוק that narrows a rule

phrases.english: After it included

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer starts from the inclusion the פסוק already made. The full reason continues in the next lines.
